additional_info.subject: ID0418687-DC/Si-D/IT-[ MP / R9 170002444 ] Problem on DC1_CableTempSensor_XD100 CRM:02684000102
additional_info.body:
Hi Riccardo, good afternoon. I hope you are doing well.
To continue with this topic, we need to update to v6.1.3 since we have updated logs for further troubleshooting.
It's also required a site visit and make the following measurements:
Remove the colored cables from XD10 (blue, orange, white and violet) and measure between:
Blue and Orange must be 1kOhm
White and Violet must be 1kOhm
If both are 1kOhm, we insert them back in the XD10 and remove from the KF14 input CCS-A IN (J4) PT1 and PT2, and measure to the respective Orange-PT1 and Violet-PT2.
If both are 1kOhm please try the following:
Replace the connector in the KF14:
Usually in these KF11/KF12/KF14, you have a spare grey connector without any connections.
If we see 1kOhm still, then we need to replace the StateMonitor.
But before this site visit, I would like to have the FW in v6.1.3 to analyse remotely what we see.
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

additional_info.subject: ID0418687-DC/Si-D/IT-[ MP / R9 170002444 ] Problem on DC1_CableTempSensor_XD100 CRM:02684000102
additional_info.body:
Hello Riccardo, good morning.
Thank you for updating to v6.1.3, here are my findings from the SECC directly:
As you can see both the Temperature sensors do not have a good reading, they both should have 1kOhm and PT1 = 1.2kOhm and PT2 = 884kOhm.
Please follow the instructions I shared in the previous email, unfortunately, remotely I cannot do anything else.
Since the values are like this I request from you another measurement/inspection:
Please check if there is water inside the plug - usually we shake the plug and try to listen closely to feel/hear anything inside the plug that shouldn't be there
Measure from CP to ground, you can see in the picture from the previous email, in KF12.
I will send this ticket to the RC-IT queue for the site support. If you require remote support please reach out to me via Teams.
Thank you!
Best regards,
Francisco
